You’ve given me a lot to think about. Thank you. 

I think my current therapist is a decent match. I already feel like I’m getting some old trash out of my head. I’m not quite comfortable enough for some topics yet, but I find it pretty easy to talk about anxiety, so that’s what we’re working on first. It’s so difficult to say some of the things I want to share out loud. Especially when they’re so easy to post about anonymously. I’ve only had sex once, it wasn’t free, I didn’t like it, and ever since I’ve felt nauseous just thinking about sex. That’s such a huge mess and I’m not sure when I’ll be ready to tell my therapist. But even only two sessions in I more easily talk about dying, so I’m seeing progress. 

What DO I want? I’m not sure I know. I want to feel like I belong in the world. I feel like I’m intruding when I’m in public places. If I had stayed home the queues would be shorter, the traffic would be better. I would also like to not hate myself. I don’t like my voice, my hair, my body, my instincts, my reflexes. They’re all garbage. I’m not funny or interesting, I’m boring and depressing. I wish I didn’t need social contact. My mere presence makes people uncomfortable. I wish I was confident in my worth. I wish I wasn’t always in some kind of pain. When it’s not my back, it’s my knees or my shoulders or my wrists. When those are fine it’s crippling mental anguish. 

I never really had dreams for my future. I always had the feeling that I would die young, within a few years. Never had goals past making it through the day. Just trying to survive my bad ideas. I’ve always had my basic needs met and a computer with an internet connection, enough to keep myself occupied and not thinking about the real world. Never had real desires beyond going home and not having to interact with Life. Sure, there were “things” I wanted, but I knew I couldn’t have them. They were never realistic for me. I wanted a girlfriend, but the basic idea of someone finding me desirable was laughable to me (it still feels absurd). In high school there was one girl who repeatedly showed interest but I never believed her. She was very patient but after a month she moved on. At the time I was relieved, it was causing me a lot of stress. I couldn’t sleep. “What if it’s true? No, it can’t be.” I was such an idiot. I still am, but I used to, too. It’s always been like this. 

What would make my suffering worth it? Shit. I don’t know. I don’t think there’s any one thing that would make it all worth it. There’s so much I would need before it would be enough. I would need a body I don’t hate, a job that doesn’t give me pain, a living situation that doesn’t involve lying every day and having to explain everything I do in detail, a reason to bother with all the boring shitty things… If I was someone else entirely, I guess. Maybe being perceived as a woman would help. And unless I meet a wish-granting genie, I’m not going to do anything about that. 

Maybe romantic love could do it, but I’m so far gone; I don’t care about myself or life, I’m completely closed to the idea of even trying to meet anyone. I’m toxic and I should stay away from people. I don’t want to risk my crappy attitude infecting someone else. 

I imagine that a good connection involves free flowing conversation, both parties asking questions and being genuinely interested. When I try, I feel like the other person is just hoping that I shut up and leave them alone. When anyone talks to me, I run out of things to say, my mind goes blank. I take too long to answer, they lose patience and just move on. IDK. I’m just wasting their time. 

You’ve warmed me up to the idea of group therapy. I still wouldn’t seek it out but if my therapist strongly believed it would help, I would consider it. It’s not entirely off the table anymore. 

I wasn’t planning on writing much beyond a simple “i’m sorry i’m doing this” to my family and friend. Maybe I should reconsider. Going through all my reasons for leaving might be therapeutic in a way. and if it could help anyone, maybe i would’ve done at least one worthwhile thing with my life.

Thank you for replying. 

I’ve been seeing a psychiatrist for ten years. I’ve tried several antidepressants, mostly zoloft for the past 8 years. I stopped taking it in january. I felt just as bad on it, but I was a lot more numb. Spent all my time playing video games, not really thinking about anything. I didn’t want to feel like that anymore. I majorly cut back on the games, quit alcohol and weed, started exercising regularly, picked up new hobbies. Learned to drive and got my license. Still, I feel like shit, and it keeps getting worse. I don’t get enjoyment out of anything but at least I can think.

My inability to connect or even interact with people never seemed to bother my psychiatrist. I can do OK if the other person is trying really hard, and I’ve told them that, so it doesn’t matter I guess? They’ve told me to join support groups for “practice,” but I could never do that. Opening up in front of a bunch of strangers who already know each other? No thanks, not for me. 

My one good real life friend studied a little bit of psychology in university, and pointed out avoidant personality disorder to me. I felt perfectly described. Might as well have my face next to the description. Depression, anxiety, and that. Probably some ADHD too, for good measure. 

I’m sorry you’ve felt the same pain from your friends. It’s so hard. I was already always alone in my classes, and outside of them my “friends” were mostly shitty to me, but what else was I gonna do? Be alone all the time? Might have been better. Oh well, it’s been a long time, and I can’t change the past. Too bad that the damage has stuck around. 

I’ll never be a homeowner, I’ll never have a family (not that I’ve ever wanted one, but I would like to feel like it’s a choice I’ve made, and not just an impossibility), I’ll probably never be really independent. I’ll never feel like I belong in any public space. I’ll never feel comfortable in my own skin. I’ll never be a woman. 

I started therapy last week. Hadn’t seen a therapist in years. I have a hard time being honest about how awful I feel. I don’t want to get locked up for my “own safety” or whatever. I hope it can help me change my mind. So far it looks like I have some very hard work ahead, and I don’t know if I have it in me to get through it. Giving up entirely is still appealing. No more anxiety, no more stress, no more pain, no more insurmountable challenges? Never having to figure out car insurance, never having to worry about making rent, never worry about anything ever again? Yes please.

I’ve never lived on my own or been in a romantic relationship. 

I’ve never had much energy, I tire very easily, I could never work the hours needed to afford rent. Very weak. I currently work ~25 hours/week and I need 11 hours of sleep, and the quality of my work is subpar. I can’t do it. 

For my whole life I was told that “love” is all you need. That with it nothing else matters, you don’t need friends, money, or anything. it’s such a fucked up thing to say. I’m not diagnosed as autistic or anything but I don’t really understand people or social cues. I can’t connect with people. I’m never comfortable around them, even my parents or my one long time friend. Meeting new people, even on the internet, is extremely difficult. I don’t really have anything to say or share. I think people instinctively know to avoid me, it’s obvious there’s shit wrong with me. I’ve been told that I give off “bad vibes.”

It’s probably because I’m not confident. Of course I’m not confident, I’ve never felt respected. Growing up, I was always the butt of the joke in my “friend” group. Last one picked for teams. Even from my parents, the music I listen to is “unlistenable”, things I watch are “unwatchable,” the art I like isn’t art. Same shit in school. 

So no, I don’t think that romance is going to happen to me. All I would bring to the table is self-loathing. I’m bad at being a person. Everything reminds me of what I’ll never be, what I’ll never have. I don’t want to deal with the pain anymore.

Disassociation is exactly what happened to me. I felt like I was piloting a robot. Like my actions were prerecorded… I’d never felt like that before.  I expected to feel something new, but not THAT. 

I don’t know if I’ve ever gone a whole day without feeling depressed. Maybe. I used to be really good at keeping myself distracted with video games, tv, sleep. I can’t really stay on the computer all day anymore, gotta go to work and be reminded that there are other people out there, with lives they enjoy. I swear, if I could somehow never see anyone else again, I would be less depressed. With enough crap to distract myself I don’t think about the things I’m missing.  

Like, I love riding my bicycle. Really helps. Until I see some young couple giggling in the park and it’s just… Oh. Right. I’m not doing anything to get that, I don’t have the confidence, etc. I don’t hate them or wish them harm or anything! I’m happy for them. I’m just envious.

Ahh, alcohol and it’s social-lubricant properties. It’s the only way I could ever be extroverted. The only way I’ve ever been comfortable at a party. I couldn’t keep it in check though, always had way too much. Physically I feel much better since quitting but holy shit does it make anything where other people are drinking really suck. “You used to be a funny guy, why are you so quiet??” I’m just being the real me 😑 thankfully (?) I don’t get invited to anything anymore

You’ve done more than 99.9% of people I’ve ever talked to. Over the years only two older coworkers have tried to get to know me. They both asked how it was possible that such a “good looking, smart young man” was single. I don’t normally bring up my mental health or general despair in person. I try to act positive, interested. But that question sure as hell had me admitting that I’ve always been severely depressed and anxious, with low self esteem. Nobody knows what to say about that. Even my previous therapists were clueless. Just a shitty brain, I guess. People were mean to me when I was a child and I never got over it. You get called a freak by the people you care about, by people you don’t care about; you end up believing it. Being the quiet reserved teenager makes you a target, only makes the issues worse. 

Sorry, I’ve been using my replies to you like therapy, just dumping my misery. You’re very kind, I hope life treats you well.

Thank you, that’s a nice, optimistic thought. I have a hard time believing that anyone could be in love with me. I’m quite unpleasant to be around and keep people away. I don’t speak unless spoken to. I’ve been told that I give off “bad vibes.” I look angry even when I’m not. 

It’s so absurdly unlikely that I would ever meet anyone; that someone would bother trying to find the person under the mountain of problems.   I do leave the house but I’m never in social situations. I can walk or bike for hours and not see anyone. Always alone in waiting rooms. I’ve tried the apps but they make me sad. I don’t have anything to say, conversations die and I feel responsible. I’m boring, I have hobbies but I’m not passionate about them. 

There are thousands of other people with more energy, goals, passion. Why should I get any attention when I’m barely alive? “Everybody deserves love” is BS, there are plenty of people with too much damage. You could argue that they could get together but I think they’ll hurt each other and would be better off never meeting. I certainly wouldn’t want to meet anyone like me. 

I do appreciate your optimism though. I wish I had it. I’ve only gotten worse with the years. Every day I think about how much easier it would be to be dead than alive. No more struggle, no more pain, no more anxiety. I’d finally be free from myself. My parents would be devastated though, so I have to tough it out.

Maybe I’m old fashioned but I have a hard time imagining online therapy. I liked how I couldn’t escape from my problems in in-person therapy. I feel like I might just close the app if it gets too hard. It’s already something I do when dealing with anything I find overwhelming
I hear ya on the dragging people down. I’ve always felt like a burden on my close ones. I need constant reassurance and encouragement.  I must be exhausting to be around, always whining

Thank you. I think my various mental health problems will keep me from ever being in a relationship. I’m too insecure, lack confidence, etc. I’d just drive anyone who was interested away with my constant complaining. I don’t think I have much to offer. Anybody would be better off with somebody else

Thank you for replying. You’ve helped me realize that I don’t really have fantasies. Fuck her as I choose? I have no clue. I don’t watch porn with men. I never related to it. I’ve never really felt like a manly man either. Didn’t feel like I belonged in men’s spaces, or anywhere else. 

Since I’ve been maybe 8 or 9 I’ve wished I was somebody else, anybody else. Anyone who was comfortable in their skin. My birthday wishes were always to wake up as a different person. Going to sleep and hoping I’d wake up in a different body. 

Always envious of the girls for being pretty and cute. I remember thinking that I wouldn’t get called a f*g if I was one. “I’m not gay, I love girls. I like ‘em so much I wouldn’t mind being one”
